originality.rationale: The exact eight-corridor, equal-shortest-path/equal-cut, conditional-cardinality-vs-Bernoulli uniform-order cutoff was not found in the published records and closest inspected mathematical/ecological sources. Prior theory supplies network-reliability polynomials and signed domination methods, but no retrieved text established the precise structural cutoff. The distinction is stated as provisional because a closely relevant 2018 full text and older reliability references were inaccessible.
residual_risks: Earlier signed-domination literature or a supplemental graph census could already contain the same exact cutoff; no independent priority verification.
The Bertrand et al. (2018) full text was unavailable; its abstract does not settle every possible implication.
The eight-edge result is only for two-terminal series-parallel multigraphs, not all ecological landscape networks.

value.rationale: Independent random corridor failures and a specified fixed-count shock are distinct landscape-risk models. The result proves a sharp and non-obvious incompatibility of their design rankings even after matching shortest path length and mincut, and establishes the first edge budget where this can occur for a coherent, widely used series-parallel construction class. This is an exact structural benchmark, not a demographic prediction.
